title: The transported mean is safe and the responder probability is not
question: When a bounded continuous outcome is transported by G-computation with a pooled normal residual, is the mean contrast safe while the responder-probability contrast is biased, and does a floor make the bias depend on the target population?
design: Source trial with arm-specific residual SDs, skewed or normal errors and a floor at 0, 10% or 25% mass, transported to targets at two shifts; normal pooled-SD, arm-specific SD, Tobit and direct logistic responder models; mean and responder contrasts at two thresholds. 24 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: Yes. With a pooled normal residual the transported mean contrast was unbiased while the responder-probability contrast was biased by up to 0.10 when the arms' dispersions differed, with opposite signs at a threshold near the median and one in the tail. Arm-specific SDs fixed it only for normal errors without a floor; Tobit fixed the floor but not skew; logistic regression of the responder indicator was unbiased everywhere. A floor biased the mean contrast by under 2% of the effect, somewhat more at the larger target shift.
findings: Dissociation confirmed: pooled-SD mean contrast within 3 MCSE without a floor; responder bias up to 0.102 at SD ratio 2.
Normal model with arm-specific SDs: responder bias up to 0.058 with a floor and 0.070 with skew.
Tobit: at most 0.003 with normal errors, 0.040 with skew; logistic responder model: at most 0.006 in every scenario.
Floor of 25%: linear mean-contrast bias -0.012 to 0.010 at shift 0.3 and -0.070 to 0.038 at shift 1.
not_answered: One source trial, no ceiling, no intervals, no ML-NMR. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target mean difference and target responder-probability differences at two thresholds
methods_compared: logistic regression of the responder indicator
